facts.text: NoMa, short for 'North of Massachusetts Avenue,' was named to echo New York City neighborhood nicknames like SoHo.
The 2004 opening of the NoMa‑Gallaudet U Metro station closed a two‑mile gap between Union Station and Rhode Island Avenue, sparking growth.
Cornelius Wendel built NoMa’s first printing factory in 1856, which the government later converted into the U.S. Government Printing Office in 1861.
In 1863, the Emancipation Proclamation was printed in NoMa’s factory, linking the neighborhood to a pivotal moment in U.S. history.
Swampoodle Park, opened in 2018, honors the 18th‑century immigrant enclave that once thrived near the area.
